lines.trans: Miss, you must not throw eggshells into the food waste.
Pardon? Why not?
Anything animals cannot eat is not food waste.
Because I worked as a teacher for so long, I just cannot overlook basic things like this.
Yes, I understand. I will not throw them in there from next time.
Right, a woman keeping house ought to know how to sort trash properly.
Then is it fine for men not to know how to throw out trash properly?

words.gloss: even if they do not know

Hey, why are you arguing out in the neighborhood?
My mind works faster than the young teachers!

examples.trans: Did you hear about this miss, young lady?
I was busy today because of miss, young lady.
Did you hear about this egg?
I was busy today because of egg.
Did you hear about this shell?
I was busy today because of shell.
Did you hear about this into food waste?
I was busy today because of into food waste.
I want to if you throw away right now.
How about trying to if you throw away together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Standard polite affirmative response; also used to acknowledge that one is listening.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Yes, I understand.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: Everyday verb for eating a meal or food; honorific equivalent is 드시다.

examples.trans: Let's eat lunch together.
Did you eat breakfast?

meanings.note: Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.
I cannot go today.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.
Did you hear about this garbage, waste?
I was busy today because of garbage, waste.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
Did you hear about this teaching profession?
I was busy today because of teaching profession.
Did you hear about this career, life?
I was busy today because of career, life.
I understand well (for a long time).
Today is a (for a long time) busy day.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: adjective like this

examples.trans: This kind of thing.
It is like this.
Did you hear about this basic?
I was busy today because of basic.

meanings.note: Softens a statement or downplays a motive.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.
I'll just stay home today.

넘어가다.gloss: to let it pass, to move on

meanings.en: to let it pass, to move on

examples.trans: I will let it slide this time.
Let's move on to the next.

meanings.en: to be unable to, cannot do
meanings.note: Expresses inability; follows a noun in 말 못하다 (cannot say).

examples.trans: I cannot swim.
I couldn't contact you because I was busy.

meanings.note: Slightly more formal/deferential variant of 네, commonly used when speaking to a boss or superior.

examples.trans: Yes, understood.
Yes, I will prepare it right away.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.
Did you hear about this female?
I was busy today because of female.
Let's while keeping house together today.
I worked hard to while keeping house yesterday too.
I understand well (properly).
Today is a (properly) busy day.

meanings.note: When used with 알다/모르다, it means knowing or not knowing a fact or how to do something.

examples.trans: I knew it would rain.
Do you know how to swim?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그러면.

examples.trans: Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?
Did you hear about this man?
I was busy today because of man.

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb: stem 모르- + -아요/-았어요 → 몰라요 / 몰랐어요.

examples.trans: I don't know well either.
I didn't realize time was passing.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.en: to be curious; to wonder about
meanings.note: Descriptive adjective in Korean; the thing wondered about takes -이/가.

examples.trans: I'm really curious about the result.
If you have anything you're curious about, please ask.
Please ask the teacher.
I will ask my mother.

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!
Did you hear about this in the neighborhood?
I was busy today because of in the neighborhood.

meanings.en: to fight; to quarrel; to argue
meanings.note: The opponent takes -와/과 or -랑.

examples.trans: Do you fight with your younger sibling often?
Don't fight with each other and get along.
It really is young compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is young and nice.

meanings.note: respectful term for teacher or senior

examples.trans: Hello teacher.
Good teacher.
Did you hear about this head, brain?
I was busy today because of head, brain.
Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.
I want to works, spins right now.
How about trying to works, spins together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!
